pr_title: sql: disable table renames across schemas
pr_body:
Fixes #50826.

As part of our goal to make `RENAME` no longer take qualified names,
this PR adjusts `RENAME` to disallow renames across schemas in
preparation for user defined schemas. Additionally, it adds a deprecated
notice for usage of qualified names in the `RENAME` command. Lastly, it
moves the behavior of `RENAME` with an unqualified name closer to
Postgres's behavior -- the unqualified name will be treated as in the
same schema and database as the input table.

Release note (sql change): Add a deprecated notice for use of `ALTER
TABLE .. RENAME` with a qualified name.

Release note (sql change): Disable using `ALTER TABLE .. RENAME` to
change the schema of a table.

Release note (sql change): Unqualified names in the target of
`ALTER TABLE ... RENAME` are treated as having the same database and
schema as the table being renamed.

issue_context.title: sql: disable renaming across schemas
issue_context.body: Postgres uses the `ALTER TABLE .. SET SCHEMA` syntax instead.
comments:
I gave this a quick go and ran into a couple troubles:
* The current temp table -> permanent table rename logic works by luck it seems. The temp schema isn't actually resolved as part of name resolution because we use `p.ResolveUncachedDatabase`, which under the hood calls `tree.ResolveTarget` which is used when the underlying object is not expected to exist. This method _doesn't_ include the temp schema when iterating, so falsely resolves all temp tables to the `public` schema. Instead, we should just use `p.getQualifiedTableName` for the table that we are renaming.
* The name resolution methods should fully resolve the temp schema in the returned table names, but this leads to inclusion of the full session ID in the temp schema name. Maybe we should strip it back out into pg_temp when returning it.

> The name resolution methods should fully resolve the temp schema in the returned table names, but this leads to inclusion of the full session ID in the temp schema name. Maybe we should strip it back out into pg_temp when returning it.

I don't think this is a problem, based on some testing with postgres. It seems like they have the same naming schema of `pg_temp_sessionid` that is resolved when a table is accessed.

review_comments: does the case for `pg_temp` not work anymore?
all of the `pg_temp`resolution still works, we just return the resolved schema name here rather than keeping it as `pg_temp` -- postgres does this as well.
